formula: CPU operating margin = 1 - (1 - baseline CPU margin) * (1 + all-in unit cost change) / (1 + realized ASP change); fixed-weight mature blend = (1 - mature Other share) * CPU margin + mature Other share * Other margin.

fixed_quantities_and_other_revenue_diagn.formula: New DCAI margin = (baseline DCAI margin + baseline CPU revenue share * ASP change) / (1 + baseline CPU revenue share * ASP change).
fixed_quantities_and_other_revenue_diagn.assumptions: CPU packages and all-in dollar costs unchanged; Other revenue and dollar profit unchanged. CPU revenue share changes mechanically when ASP changes. This repairs the fixed-mix simplification in the separate grid.

limitations: Other profitability and standalone CPU profitability are not disclosed. This reexpresses an existing conditional margin illustration, not a new forecast.
Holding all-in cost per CPU implicitly holds allocated OpEx per unit; real fixed cost leverage, volumes, customer/SKU mix and transfer prices can differ.
Intel 3 cost learning is a manufacturing cost metric, not a proportional reduction in all DCAI costs; it cannot be dropped directly into this grid.
The conditional grid holds mature Other revenue share fixed. The separate fixed-quantities diagnostic allows share weights to change mechanically with ASP.

capacity_calendar_diagnostic.equation: Annual good-package factor = starting run-rate carryover * calendar-weighted capacity factor * yield/utilization factor / resource use per good-package factor; the tightest wafer/substrate/assembly stage binds.
capacity_calendar_diagnostic.interpretation: An illustrative 40% capacity addition active for a full half-year contributes 20% annual capacity if the other half is unchanged; a linear ramp from 0 to 40% during the half contributes 10%. Exact Intel capacity units, timing, baseline and mix are not disclosed, so this is not an Intel shipment estimate.
capacity_calendar_diagnostic.warning: Management's reported ~40% substrate capacity remark is from Q&A transcriptions; prepared remarks directly verify bottlenecks but not that numerical capacity specification. Do not assert capacity equals CPU units.
